2	name: mvi-architecture
3	description: Model-View-Intent architecture patterns for Android with unidirectional data flow, state management, and side effects.
4	---
5	
6	# MVI Architecture
7	
8	Unidirectional data flow architecture for Android.
9	
10	## Core Concepts
11	
12	```
13	Intent → ViewModel → State → UI
14	   ↑                        │
15	   └────────────────────────┘
16	```
17	
18	## State
19	
20	```kotlin
21	@Immutable
22	data class HomeState(
23	    val isLoading: Boolean = false,
24	    val items: List<Item> = emptyList(),
25	    val error: ErrorState? = null,
26	    val searchQuery: String = ""
27	) {
28	    sealed interface ErrorState {
29	        data class Network(val message: String) : ErrorState
30	        data object Unauthorized : ErrorState
31	    }
32	}
33	```
34	
35	## Intent
36	
37	```kotlin
38	sealed interface HomeIntent {
39	    object LoadItems : HomeIntent
40	    object Refresh : HomeIntent
41	    data class Search(val query: String) : HomeIntent
42	    data class ItemClicked(val id: String) : HomeIntent
43	    object ClearError : HomeIntent
44	}
45	```
46	
47	## Side Effects
48	
49	```kotlin
50	sealed interface HomeSideEffect {
51	    data class NavigateToDetail(val itemId: String) : HomeSideEffect
52	    data class ShowSnackbar(val message: String) : HomeSideEffect
53	    object NavigateToLogin : HomeSideEffect
54	}
55	```
56	
57	## ViewModel
58	
59	```kotlin
60	class HomeViewModel(
61	    private val getItemsUseCase: GetItemsUseCase
62	) : ViewModel() {
63	
64	    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(HomeState())
65	    val state: StateFlow<HomeState> = _state.asStateFlow()
66	
67	    private val _sideEffects = Channel<HomeSideEffect>(Channel.BUFFERED)
68	    val sideEffects: Flow<HomeSideEffect> = _sideEffects.receiveAsFlow()
69	
70	    fun onIntent(intent: HomeIntent) {
71	        when (intent) {
72	            is HomeIntent.LoadItems -> loadItems()
73	            is HomeIntent.Refresh -> loadItems(refresh = true)
74	            is HomeIntent.Search -> search(intent.query)
75	            is HomeIntent.ItemClicked -> {
76	                viewModelScope.launch {
77	                    _sideEffects.send(HomeSideEffect.NavigateToDetail(intent.id))
78	                }
79	            }
80	            is HomeIntent.ClearError -> _state.update { it.copy(error = null) }
81	        }
82	    }
83	
84	    private fun loadItems(refresh: Boolean = false) {
85	        viewModelScope.launch {
86	            if (!refresh) _state.update { it.copy(isLoading = true) }
87	            
88	            getItemsUseCase()
89	                .onSuccess { items ->
90	                    _state.update { it.copy(isLoading = false, items = items, error = null) }
91	                }
92	                .onFailure { error ->
93	                    _state.update { it.copy(isLoading = false, error = mapError(error)) }
94	                }
95	        }
96	    }
97	    
98	    private fun mapError(error: Throwable): HomeState.ErrorState {
99	        return when (error) {
100	            is UnauthorizedException -> HomeState.ErrorState.Unauthorized
101	            else -> HomeState.ErrorState.Network(error.message ?: "Unknown error")
102	        }
103	    }
104	}
105	```
106	
107	## UI Integration
108	
109	```kotlin
110	@Composable
111	fun HomeScreen(
112	    viewModel: HomeViewModel = koinViewModel(),
113	    onNavigateToDetail: (String) -> Unit,
114	    onNavigateToLogin: () -> Unit
115	) {
116	    val state by viewModel.state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
117	    val snackbarHostState = remember { SnackbarHostState() }
118	    
119	    // Handle side effects
120	    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
121	        viewModel.sideEffects.collect { effect ->
122	            when (effect) {
123	                is HomeSideEffect.NavigateToDetail -> onNavigateToDetail(effect.itemId)
124	                is HomeSideEffect.ShowSnackbar -> snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(effect.message)
125	                is HomeSideEffect.NavigateToLogin -> onNavigateToLogin()
126	            }
127	        }
128	    }
129	    
130	    // Load data
131	    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
132	        viewModel.onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems)
133	    }
134	    
135	    HomeContent(
136	        state = state,
137	        onIntent = viewModel::onIntent,
138	        snackbarHostState = snackbarHostState
139	    )
140	}
141	
142	@Composable
143	private fun HomeContent(
144	    state: HomeState,
145	    onIntent: (HomeIntent) -> Unit,
146	    snackbarHostState: SnackbarHostState
147	) {
148	    Scaffold(
149	        snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState) }
150	    ) { padding ->
151	        when {
152	            state.isLoading -> LoadingIndicator()
153	            state.error != null -> ErrorContent(
154	                error = state.error,
155	                onRetry = { onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems) }
156	            )
157	            else -> ItemList(
158	                items = state.items,
159	                onItemClick = { onIntent(HomeIntent.ItemClicked(it)) }
160	            )
161	        }
162	    }
163	}
164	```
165	
166	## Testing
167	
168	```kotlin
169	@Test
170	fun `when LoadItems succeeds, state contains items`() = runTest {
171	    val items = listOf(Item("1", "Test"))
172	    coEvery { getItemsUseCase() } returns Result.success(items)
173	    
174	    viewModel.state.test {
175	        awaitItem() // Initial
176	        
177	        viewModel.onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems)
178	        
179	        awaitItem().isLoading shouldBe true
180	        awaitItem().items shouldBe items
181	    }
182	}
183	```
184	
185	---
186	
187	**Remember**: MVI = predictable state, testable logic, debuggable flow.

2	name: android-patterns

4	---
5	
6	# Android Development Patterns
7	
8	Modern Android patterns with Kotlin, coroutines, and functional programming.
9	
10	## Kotlin Idioms
11	
12	### Immutability
13	
14	```kotlin
15	// ✅ Prefer val over var
16	val name: String = "John"
17	
18	// ✅ Immutable collections
19	val items: List<Item> = listOf(item1, item2)
20	
21	// ✅ Data class with copy
22	data class User(val id: String, val name: String)
23	val updatedUser = user.copy(name = "Jane")
24	```
25	
26	### Null Safety
27	
28	```kotlin
29	// ✅ Safe call
30	val length = name?.length
31	
32	// ✅ Elvis operator
33	val name = nullableName ?: "Unknown"
34	
35	// ✅ let for null checks
36	nullableUser?.let { user ->
37	    processUser(user)
38	}
39	
40	// ✅ Early return with null check
41	fun processUser(user: User?) {
42	    user ?: return
43	    // user is smart-cast to non-null
44	}
45	```
46	
47	### Scope Functions
48	
49	```kotlin
50	// let - Transform and return
51	val result = nullable?.let { transform(it) }
52	
53	// run - Configure and return result
54	val result = service.run {
55	    configure()
56	    execute()
57	}
58	
59	// with - Operate on object
60	with(binding) {
61	    title.text = "Title"
62	    subtitle.text = "Subtitle"
63	}
64	
65	// apply - Configure and return self
66	val user = User().apply {
67	    name = "John"
68	    email = "john@example.com"
69	}
70	
71	// also - Side effects, return self
72	val user = User().also {
73	    logger.log("Created user: ${it.id}")
74	}
75	```
76	
77	### Extensions
78	
79	```kotlin
80	// ✅ Extension functions
81	fun String.isValidEmail(): Boolean {
82	    return android.util.Patterns.EMAIL_ADDRESS.matcher(this).matches()
83	}
84	
85	// ✅ Extension properties
86	val Context.screenWidth: Int
87	    get() = resources.displayMetrics.widthPixels
88	
89	// Usage
90	if (email.isValidEmail()) { ... }
91	val width = context.screenWidth
92	```
93	
94	## Lifecycle Patterns
95	
96	### ViewModel
97	
98	```kotlin
99	class HomeViewModel(
100	    private val repository: HomeRepository,
101	    savedStateHandle: SavedStateHandle
102	) : ViewModel() {
103	
104	    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(HomeState())
105	    val state: StateFlow<HomeState> = _state.asStateFlow()
106	    
107	    init {
108	        loadData()
109	    }
110	    
111	    private fun loadData() {
112	        viewModelScope.launch {
113	            _state.update { it.copy(isLoading = true) }
114	            
115	            repository.getItems()
116	                .onSuccess { items -> _state.update { it.copy(items = items, isLoading = false) } }
117	                .onFailure { error -> _state.update { it.copy(error = error.message, isLoading = false) } }
118	        }
119	    }
120	}
121	```
122	
123	### Lifecycle-aware Collection
124	
125	```kotlin
126	@Composable
127	fun HomeScreen(viewModel: HomeViewModel = koinViewModel()) {
128	    val state by viewModel.state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
129	    
130	    HomeContent(state = state)
131	}
132	```
133	
134	## Functional Patterns
135	
136	### Result Type
137	
138	```kotlin
139	// ✅ Use Result for operations that can fail
140	suspend fun fetchUser(id: String): Result<User> = runCatching {
141	    api.getUser(id).toDomain()
142	}
143	
144	// ✅ Chain operations
145	repository.fetchUser(id)
146	    .map { it.profile }
147	    .mapCatching { decryptProfile(it) }
148	    .onSuccess { displayProfile(it) }
149	    .onFailure { showError(it) }
150	```
151	
152	### Higher-Order Functions
153	
154	```kotlin
155	// ✅ Pass functions as parameters
156	fun <T> retry(
157	    times: Int,
158	    block: suspend () -> T
159	): T {
160	    repeat(times - 1) {
161	        try { return block() }
162	        catch (e: Exception) { delay(1000) }
163	    }
164	    return block() // Last attempt
165	}
166	
167	// Usage
168	val result = retry(3) { api.fetchData() }
169	```
170	
171	### Sealed Classes
172	
173	```kotlin
174	sealed interface UiState<out T> {
175	    data object Loading : UiState<Nothing>
176	    data class Success<T>(val data: T) : UiState<T>
177	    data class Error(val message: String) : UiState<Nothing>
178	}
179	
180	// Exhaustive when
181	when (state) {
182	    is UiState.Loading -> LoadingIndicator()
183	    is UiState.Success -> Content(state.data)
184	    is UiState.Error -> ErrorMessage(state.message)
185	}
186	```
187	
188	## Resource Management
189	
190	### Context Extensions
191	
192	```kotlin
193	fun Context.dp(value: Int): Int = 
194	    (value * resources.displayMetrics.density).toInt()
195	
196	fun Context.showToast(message: String) {
197	    Toast.makeText(this, message, Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
198	}
199	```
200	
201	### String Resources
202	
203	```kotlin
204	// strings.xml
205	<string name="welcome_message">Welcome, %1$s!</string>
206	
207	// Usage
208	stringResource(R.string.welcome_message, userName)
209	```
210	
211	---
212	
213	**Remember**: Kotlin is concise. Embrace its idioms for cleaner, safer code.

52	For a **new** project or feature with no established convention. In existing code, match what's already there — see *Reuse the project's existing mechanism* below.
53	
54	The UI layer is MVVM with an MVI-style state/effect split:
55	
56	- **One immutable `UiState` per screen**, exposed as `StateFlow<UiState>` and structured with the four buckets below. The content composable renders it and emits callbacks — nothing else.
57	- **One effects stream for fire-once imperatives** — navigate, snackbar/toast, scroll-to, share-sheet, haptics. Collect it in a `LaunchedEffect` (lifecycle-scoped via `repeatOnLifecycle`), never `collectAsStateWithLifecycle`. Channel-vs-`SharedFlow` rationale: `android-skills:kotlin-flows`.
58	- **State vs effect — "does it survive a config change?"** Anything still true after rotation / process death is **state** (an error to show = a field in `UiState`); anything the UI runs once and forgets is an **effect**. This is the `durable-state-over-events` rule in `compose/references/state-management.md`: keep durable things in state; the effect stream is only for one-shot imperatives.
59	- **Promote callbacks to a `@Stable Actions` interface at ~4–5+** (or when the same set is threaded through several composable layers). 63

65	    data class NavigateTo(val id: String) : FooEffect
66	    data class ShowSnackbar(val message: String) : FooEffect
67	}
68

73	}

80	    val effects = _effects.receiveAsFlow()

88	    val uiState by viewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
89	    val lifecycle = LocalLifecycleOwner.current.lifecycle
90	    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
91	        lifecycle.repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {
92	            viewModel.effects.collect { effect ->

106	## Four-bucket state modeling
107	
108	Screens with rich interactions (forms, calculators, multi-step wizards) get unmanageable when state is one flat `data class`. Slice `UiState` into four explicit buckets, and **derive computed values as class properties, not constructor parameters**:

112	    // 1. Editable input — what the user types
113	    val email: String = "",
114	    val cardNumber: String = "",
115	    // 3. Persisted snapshot — last value read from the repository / stored cross-screen
116	    val savedShippingAddress: Address? = null,
117	    // 4. Transient UI-only — flags that must NOT survive the screen
118	    val isSubmitting: Boolean = false,
119	    val showCardScannerOverlay: Boolean = false,
120	) {
121	    // 2. Derived — getters, NOT constructor params, so no caller can copy() into an
122	    //    inconsistent state (e.g. emailValid = false next to a valid email).
123	    val emailValid: Boolean get() = email.isValidEmail()

132	Before adding any new mechanism — an event dispatcher, an effects `Channel`/`SharedFlow`, a use-case layer, or a parallel state field — open a sibling ViewModel in the same feature and reuse what's already there. 6	# Modularization
7	
8	**Declare everything at the lowest visibility that still compiles.** Start `private`; widen to `internal` only when another file in the *same module* needs it; widen to `public` only when a *different module* actually consumes it. Kotlin defaults to `public`, and in a multi-module project that default is usually wrong — a `public` symbol joins the module's API surface: it leaks implementation across the boundary and you are then obliged to keep it stable.
9	
10	- Public interface as the module's API → the interface is `public`; its **implementation class stays `internal`** (DI-bound, never named from another module).
11	- Mapper / helper / extension / constant / UI-state holder used only inside the module → `internal` (or `private` if a single file uses it). "Rendered by a composable in this module" does **not** require `public` — `internal` is visible to the whole module.
12	- Member used only within its class → `private`.
13	
14	Widening a symbol to `public` is a decision, not a default: confirm a real cross-module consumer first.

The key insight is that init{} actually avoids the rotation-reload bug that LaunchedEffect introduces — so this isn't just stylistic divergence, one approach is technically more correct. That solidifies the finding. I'll write this up with line numbers to keep the reasoning tight.

contradictionVerdicts.topic: How to collect the one-shot effects/side-effects Channel in Compose (lifecycle scoping)
contradictionVerdicts.reasoning: Verified in the files. ahmed mvi-architecture/SKILL.md lines 120-128 collect the effects flow in a plain `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.sideEffects.collect { ... } }` with NO repeatOnLifecycle. rcosteira android-dev/SKILL.md line 57 explicitly mandates the opposite: 'Collect it in a `LaunchedEffect` (lifecycle-scoped via `repeatOnLifecycle`), never `collectAsStateWithLifecycle`', and the example at lines 90-99 wraps the collect in `lifecycle.repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) { viewModel.effects.collect { ... } }`. Both sides use the same source stream — `Channel(Channel.BUFFERED).receiveAsFlow()` (ahmed lines 67-68; rcosteira lines 79-81) — so the only divergence is the collection site, and it is a genuine opposing-pattern conflict. With plain LaunchedEffect the composition stays alive while the Activity is STOPPED, so an effect emitted while backgrounded is consumed immediately (off-screen navigation/snackbar); rcosteira's repeatOnLifecycle cancels collection when STOPPED so the buffered Channel replays on resume. This is the exact behavior rcosteira's rationale depends on, and ahmed's template defeats it. Real conflict on the same decision.

contradictionVerdicts.topic: Where the initial data load is triggered (UI composable vs ViewModel init)
contradictionVerdicts.reasoning: Both sources are ahmed and the code differs exactly as claimed. mvi-architecture/SKILL.md lines 131-133 trigger the load from the UI: `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems) }`. android-patterns/SKILL.md lines 107-109 trigger it inside the ViewModel: `init { loadData() }`. These are genuinely different trigger sites for the same 'load the screen's data on first display' decision, and they behave differently across configuration change: `init{}` runs once per (retained) ViewModel and survives rotation, whereas `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` re-runs when the composition is recreated on rotation, re-issuing LoadItems and re-fetching. It is a real within-author divergence (and one that is not purely stylistic, since the init approach avoids the rotation-reload). Note the MVI 'dispatch intent from the UI' idiom is internally consistent with MVI philosophy while init{} is the plain-MVVM idiom, but as concrete emitted code for the same task the two skills conflict.

contradictionVerdicts.topic: Default dependency-injection framework for greenfield ViewModel/Compose code
contradictionVerdicts.reasoning: The code divergence is real: ahmed mvi-architecture line 112 and android-patterns line 127 both use `koinViewModel()`; rcosteira android-dev line 20 names the house default 'DI: Hilt + KSP (or android-skills:koin when the project uses Koin)' and the greenfield example at line 87 uses `hiltViewModel()`. So for a greenfield project the two clusters would emit opposing DI wiring (Koin vs Hilt). However it is a divergent DEFAULT, not an absolute contradiction: (1) rcosteira explicitly permits Koin when the project already uses it, and (2) neither ahmed skill contains any prescriptive DI rule or 'house defaults' section — Koin appears only implicitly in example code, never stated as a mandated default. So claimA ('Both ahmed skills use Koin unconditionally as THE default') is an inference from examples rather than a stated rule. Real greenfield divergence, softened by rcosteira's hedge and the absence of an explicit ahmed prescription — hence PARTIAL.

bugVerdicts.description: retry() declared as plain (non-suspend) fun but calls delay(1000) and invokes a suspend lambda block(); does not compile.
bugVerdicts.reasoning: Verified android-patterns/SKILL.md lines 156-165. `fun <T> retry(times: Int, block: suspend () -> T): T` is NOT marked `suspend`, yet its body calls `block()` (typed `suspend () -> T`) and `delay(1000)` (a suspend function). Both can only be invoked from a coroutine or another suspend function, so the compiler rejects this ('Suspend function should be called only from a coroutine or another suspend function'). The `repeat { }` lambda is inline so its body runs in retry's own non-suspend context — no rescue. Signature must be `suspend fun retry(...)`. It is presented under the recommended 'Higher-Order Functions' section. Genuine, unambiguous compile error. Critical severity is fair.

bugVerdicts.description: retry() catches Exception, swallowing CancellationException and breaking structured concurrency; the loop keeps retrying/delaying after its scope is cancelled.
bugVerdicts.reasoning: The factual half is true: android-patterns lines 160-163 `catch (e: Exception) { delay(1000) }` does catch CancellationException (on JVM it extends Exception), and the idiomatic fix is a preceding `catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` — which the sibling rcosteira skill literally cites at line 140 ('// rethrow first — a broad catch would swallow CancellationException'). But the described FAILURE SCENARIO is inaccurate for this specific code: after the catch, `delay(1000)` executes, and in a cancelled coroutine `delay` is itself a cancellation point that immediately re-throws CancellationException (it does NOT wait 1000ms and does NOT loop). So genuine job-cancellation propagates out of retry via the delay rather than being swallowed into an endless retry loop. The residual real defect is only the missing CancellationException rethrow (a spurious, still-active-scope CancellationException from e.g. a nested withTimeout would be treated as retryable). Real anti-pattern, but the stated consequence ('keeps retrying and delaying after cancellation') does not occur. Also moot in isolation since bug #1 means it never compiles.

bugVerdicts.description: fetchUser() wraps a suspend network call in runCatching, catching CancellationException and converting a cancelled call to Result.failure so cancellation never propagates.
bugVerdicts.reasoning: Verified android-patterns lines 140-142: `suspend fun fetchUser(id: String): Result<User> = runCatching { api.getUser(id).toDomain() }`, marked '✅' at line 139. `runCatching` catches Throwable, including CancellationException. `api.getUser(id)` is a cancellable suspend call; if the coroutine is cancelled during it, the CancellationException is captured into `Result.failure` and the function returns NORMALLY — unlike the retry case there is no subsequent cancellation point (no delay) to re-throw, so cancellation is genuinely swallowed. The caller chain (lines 145-150: `.onFailure { showError(it) }`) would then render an error instead of respecting cancellation, breaking structured concurrency. Well-documented Kotlin anti-pattern; correct form is try/catch that rethrows CancellationException. Major severity fair.

bugVerdicts.description: Side-effects Channel collected in plain LaunchedEffect(Unit) with no repeatOnLifecycle, so effects (navigation, snackbar) fire while the screen is backgrounded.
bugVerdicts.reasoning: Verified mvi-architecture lines 119-128. The collector `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.sideEffects.collect { ... NavigateToDetail/ShowSnackbar/NavigateToLogin ... } }` has no lifecycle gating. The composition stays alive while the Activity is STOPPED, so an effect emitted while backgrounded (e.g. an async result completing after the user backgrounds the app) is delivered immediately: navigation stacks off-screen / a snackbar shows to nobody. The buffered Channel only behaves correctly if collection pauses when backgrounded, which is exactly what rcosteira mandates via repeatOnLifecycle (lines 90-99) and what its buffer-and-replay rationale (line 57) requires. Real, recognized lifecycle defect. It is a subtle correctness/best-practice issue rather than a guaranteed crash, so 'major' is on the strong side but defensible.

bugVerdicts.description: Initial load dispatched from LaunchedEffect(Unit) re-fires on activity/composition recreation, reloading data on every rotation.
bugVerdicts.reasoning: Verified mvi-architecture lines 131-133: `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems) }`. On configuration change the Activity/composition is recreated by default, so LaunchedEffect(Unit) enters composition fresh and re-runs, re-dispatching LoadItems. loadItems() (lines 84-96) then sets isLoading=true and re-fetches, replacing state.items on the already-populated (retained) ViewModel — a redundant reload/spinner flash per rotation. A ViewModel `init{}` block (as android-patterns line 107 uses) runs once and survives config change, avoiding this. Real behavior; the defect only manifests on config change and the fetch may be cheap if cached, so 'minor' is the correct severity.

missedIssues: Error-modeling inconsistency the finder missed: ahmed android-patterns/SKILL.md line 117 stores the raw throwable message directly in UI state (`.onFailure { error -> _state.update { it.copy(error = error.message, ...) } }`). This contradicts (a) ahmed's OWN mvi-architecture skill, which maps errors to a rich domain `ErrorState` sealed type via `mapError()` (lines 28-32, 98-103), and (b) rcosteira android-dev line 23 which mandates 'Errors: mapped to a domain type at the repository boundary — platform exceptions never leak past it'. A raw String error message is a within-cluster inconsistency and a soft contradiction with rcosteira's domain-error rule.

ahmed android-patterns/SKILL.md line 100 injects `savedStateHandle: SavedStateHandle` into the ViewModel constructor but never uses it anywhere in the shown example — a dead/unused constructor parameter in code presented as a recommended pattern.

The ahmed mvi-architecture test (lines 168-182) references `viewModel` with no shown instantiation/@Before setup, and asserts `awaitItem().isLoading shouldBe true` then `awaitItem().items shouldBe items`. Because `_state` is a StateFlow (which conflates rapid updates), the intermediate isLoading=true emission may be conflated away under a test dispatcher, making the first assertion brittle. Speculative/minor, but the finder did not examine the test's correctness at all.

Both are legitimately confirmable, but they are double-counted rather than independent findings.
